selected_primary_idea.title: CortexSwitch: Reciprocal Multiplex Causal Mapping of Human-Lineage Cortical Developmental Modules
selected_primary_idea.scientific_object: Early cortical progenitor-state transitions in human and chimpanzee stem-cell-derived organoid systems
selected_primary_idea.central_hypothesis: A small, evidence-qualified combination of human-lineage duplicated-gene and regulatory changes shifts a conserved progenitor-to-neuron developmental transition through a measurable molecular program; the effect requires reciprocal, line-aware, fidelity-qualified evidence.
candidate_classes: state-active HAR or human-specific 3D-contact regulatory candidates
falsification_conditions: No reciprocal sign-consistent perturbation effect across qualified lines.
No correspondence between candidate perturbation, molecular mediator, and predeclared cell-state endpoint.
Apparent result vanishes under line, batch, regional-identity, or developmental-alignment controls.
Combination effect is no better than matched single-candidate and neutral-edit controls after multiplicity correction.
selected_primary_idea.claim_ceiling: Conditional causal support for a tested cortical developmental module; no claim about human cognition or complete species uniqueness.
